chalisa.do1: Bowing to the feet of Śrī Guru and propitiating Sarasvatī and Gaṇeśa,
I tell the pure fame of Rāmdev, by hearing which sins are destroyed.
chalisa.do2: The lord of Dvārakā came and took incarnation as a man;
there was rejoicing in Ajmal's house, and cries of victory in the world.
chalisa.cau1: Victory, victory to you, Rāmdev, king of the gods, son of Ajmal, whose māyā is wondrous.
chalisa.cau2: You are a form of Viṣṇu, lord of gods and men, supremely glorious, the indweller who knows all hearts.
chalisa.cau3: Taking incarnation, you came down to the earth, and were called the crest-jewel of the Tanwar clan.
chalisa.cau4: You accomplished all the works of the saints, and destroyed the dānavas, the daityas and the wicked.
chalisa.cau5: The first miracle (parcā) you gave to your father: you made milk appear in the pot-stand.
chalisa.cau6: Footprints of kuṅkuma appeared at the gateway the moment the Lord revealed himself in the cradle.
chalisa.cau7: Your mother received the second miracle: when the milk was boiling over, you lifted the pot.
chalisa.cau8: The townspeople received the third: even a horse made of rags was made fit to ride.
chalisa.cau9: In the fourth miracle you slew Bhairava, the demon, and removed the suffering of your devotees.
chalisa.cau10: Ratnā received the fifth: going to Puṅgal, the Lord freed him from the snare.
chalisa.cau11: Vijaysiṃh received the sixth: his city burned, and he came to you for refuge.
chalisa.cau12: Sugnā received the seventh: her dead son came running back, laughing.
chalisa.cau13: Bauhit received the eighth: he went to a foreign land and brought back much wealth.
chalisa.cau14: You rescued his boat as it sank in a whirlpool; at his call the incarnate Lord appeared and arrived.
chalisa.cau15: Vīram received the ninth, when a merchant came and told him of his plight.
chalisa.cau16: A banjārā received the tenth: all his sugar candy became briny salt.
chalisa.cau17: The eleventh was your grace: all the salt became sugar candy again.
chalisa.cau18: In the twelfth miracle you struck the ground with your foot and created a dear, spotless pond.
chalisa.cau19: In the thirteenth the pīrs came; you brought their bowls and accomplished their purpose.
chalisa.cau20: Jāmbho received the fourteenth: you had the water of his own pond made salty.
chalisa.cau21: Then you showed the fifteenth: the Lord had the Rāma Sarovara dug.
chalisa.cau22: Harbū received the sixteenth: receiving your darśana, he rejoiced exceedingly.
chalisa.cau23: Harjī received the seventeenth: milk came to the teats of a he-goat.
chalisa.cau24: You brought water to the dry pond, and gave Harjī knowledge of the Self.
chalisa.cau25: The hākim received the eighteenth: as he slept, you rolled him onto the ground.
chalisa.cau26: Dalajī received the nineteenth: he obtained a son and rejoiced at heart.
chalisa.cau27: The merchant's wife received the twentieth: the Lord came when he heard her voice choked with feeling.
chalisa.cau28: At once you brought the merchant back to life, and gave your renowned devotee the boon of fearlessness.
chalisa.cau29: The thief who received the twenty-first went blind and received the fruit of his deeds.
chalisa.cau30: In the twenty-second the Mirzās came to know you: the Lord pierced all seven iron griddles.
chalisa.cau31: The emperor received the twenty-third: never again did he trouble a devotee.
chalisa.cau32: The Bakhśī received the twenty-fourth: his dead son rose in a moment and ran.
chalisa.cau33: Whenever anyone remembered you, you came then and gave him darśana.
chalisa.cau34: Hearing a devotee's call, you hasten in eagerness; mounted on Līlā, you come quickly.
chalisa.cau35: Those who sing the Lord's divine play gain the fruit of the works their hearts desire.
chalisa.cau36: Whoever hears or recites this chālīsā has all his troubles cut away.
chalisa.cau37: Victory, victory, victory to you, Lord, who take on divine play; your glory is boundless.
chalisa.cau38: I am a fool: what virtues of yours can I sing? Where shall I find wisdom like Sarasvatī's?
chalisa.cau39: There is not the least trace of wisdom or strength in my heart; I have composed this chālīsā as far as my understanding goes.
chalisa.cau40: All your servants are in your refuge; Lord, keep my honour.
